subject.title: Low-risk: Docker Go template injection, thread-ownership URL path injection, TLS env bypass

question: Should OpenClaw split the Docker/thread input-validation fixes from the Gateway/Control UI break-glass policy change, or narrow all break-glass behavior now?
rationale: Current docs and tests intentionally support the WebSocket and Control UI escape hatches, while repository policy treats fallback, config, and security-boundary changes as compatibility-sensitive owner decisions.

options.title: Split narrow fixes first
options.body: Land Docker label validation and thread URL encoding in a focused repair, while keeping the Gateway and Control UI break-glass policy change under explicit security review.

options.title: Narrow all break-glass paths
options.body: Replace hostname-wide private WebSocket allowance and broad Control UI dangerous flags with a narrower allowlist or verified-private mechanism, accepting the migration, docs, and upgrade work.

options.title: Keep policy, harden helpers only
options.body: Treat current Gateway and Control UI break-glass behavior as intentional operator policy and only harden the Docker and thread helper boundaries.

recommendation.title: Split narrow fixes first
recommendation.body: Land Docker label validation and thread URL encoding in a focused repair, while keeping the Gateway and Control UI break-glass policy change under explicit security review.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the clearest history signal for the private WebSocket policy decision because live metadata shows he merged the policy PR.
